ca_rock_garden_valley_middle.blurb: A quiet pocket of Joshua Tree National Park in the Lost Horse district, sitting between the left and right sections of Rock Garden Valley. Nearly everything here is single-pitch trad with a single top-rope line, and the grades run from easy fifth class up to a lone 5.11, with 5.10 the most common level. The walls face east, so you get sun early and shade by afternoon. It sees far fewer parties than the left side, which makes it a good pick for a peaceful day of crack and face climbing. Expect uneven, rocky footing near the base.
ca_rock_garden_valley_middle.approach: A trail leaves the parking area and turns into a boulder scramble; keep going past the foot of the right-side wall to reach this one. Allow roughly 15 to 25 minutes on foot.

ca_b_zippity_do_dah_buttress.blurb: A small buttress tucked under the southeast side of Fresno Dome in the western Sierra, at around 7,000 feet. Where the dome itself is known for long multi-pitch lines, this spot is the place for short, single-pitch climbing: nine bolted routes and two trad lines, mostly from 5.7 to 5.11. The bolts were replaced with stainless hardware in 2021 and the anchors sit within a half rope length. It makes a handy warm-up or a half-day outing, and the higher elevation keeps it fairly cool in summer.

ca_houda_south.blurb: A stretch of beach bouldering on the north coast near Trinidad, covering the boulders, small coves and low cliffs that run from Houda Point toward Moonstone. All eleven problems are boulders, mostly easy to moderate, from V0 through V3, with a couple of harder ones up to the V5 range. Landings depend on the tide and on how much sand is in: low water with sand piled up is ideal, while winter can leave a jumble of cobbles. Reach it by taking the stairs down to the beach, then walking a short distance along the sand to the rocks.

ca_central_area_aka_edge_rock.blurb: The middle cluster of black basalt formations at Indian Joe Caves, in Sunol Regional Wilderness in the East Bay hills. Most climbs here are top-rope setups, with a few bolted lines and a single trad crack, running from about 5.7 up to the low 5.12s, and the 5.10s and 5.11s are the bulk of it. Formations can be climbed from several sides. Getting to the anchors takes some scrambling around Little Eiger, so it suits parties comfortable with easy exposed moves. Black rock soaks up heat, so summer afternoons in the sun are punishing.

ca_8_secret_tower.blurb: A hidden wall at Marble Caves, high on a ridge above the South Fork of the Trinity River in the far northwest of the state. It holds eleven routes on limestone, nine bolted and two set up for top rope, running from 5.8 into the 5.11 range, with 5.10 and 5.11 making up most of the list. The base is reported to stay cool and breezy, so it works as a refuge when other walls are baking. It sits in the gully behind the Visionary Buttress, between the Up and Down Wall and the Sunset Wall, and the rocky gully path can be rough.

ca_cockroach_crag_climbs.blurb: A squat brown outcrop in the Lost Horse district of Joshua Tree National Park, found just to the right of the Classic Corner formation. The eleven routes are mostly traditional with a pair of top-rope lines, from 5.6 up to about 5.11, with the heaviest concentration around 5.8 to 5.10. The stone is not the park's best: holds can be loose and some are said to pull off, so bring a helmet and test everything. Every line can be top-roped by walking up a gully on either side. The walk-in crosses talus and boulders.
